answer: The vine graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the quartz audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the shale checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 2 times its size, so a group of 92 keys loses far more than 92 single identities would. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
